title: Responsible AI, Fairness, and Explainability in Autonomous Security Systems
source: AI Ethics and Governance Review, Vol. 8, 2024
content: Autonomous decision systems deployed in high-stakes cybersecurity domains necessitate rigorous fairness, transparency, and explainability standards. Black-box predictive models obscure the underlying causal rationale for threat categorization, hindering post-incident forensic investigations. Incorporating explainable artificial intelligence techniques, such as local interpretable model-agnostic explanations and Shapley additive explanations, allows security operators to inspect feature attributions and identify potential model bias. Furthermore, autonomous orchestration frameworks must enforce algorithmic guardrails, continuous model monitoring, and human-in-the-loop validation to mitigate catastrophic drift and ensure alignment with institutional ethical policies.
